findings.title: cook_method default is raw_html, converts all existing posts
findings.body: Migration sets default: 1, null:false. Post.cook_methods is Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) so regular=0 and raw_html=1. Every existing row backfilled with 1 will hit `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in app/models/post.rb and bypass the markdown/sanitize pipeline, rendering raw markdown source as cooked HTML.

findings.title: raw_html cook bypass returns unsanitized remote HTML
findings.body: Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for cook_method raw_html. TopicEmbed.import/import_remote store RSS/Readability HTML and Disqus content with that flag and render it with `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb. There is no sanitization, so arbitrary <script>, <iframe>, on* attributes from a feed or scraped page become persistent XSS for every viewer of the topic and embed.

findings.title: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in JS
findings.body: The layout interpolates `<%= request.referer %>` inside a single-quoted JavaScript string without escaping. Referer is attacker-controlled request header, so a value like `');alert(1);//` breaks out of the string and executes script in the embed origin.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin uses full referer URL instead of origin
findings.body: The second argument to parent.postMessage is `'<%= request.referer %>'` which includes path/query. Browsers require an origin of the form scheme://host:port or *, so delivery with a full URL never matches and auto-resize breaks. It also leaks the embedding page path.

findings.title: Reversed substring origin check on postMessage
findings.body: postMessageReceived does `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` instead of comparing origins for equality. Any e.origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl (for example a one-character string like `/` or `:`) passes, while the correct check must verify e.origin equals the Discourse origin. This lets a malicious frame resize/inject messages.

findings.title: Unsafe open() on admin-configured feed URL
findings.body: Code calls `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` via Kernel#open from open-uri. Kernel#open interprets a leading `|` as a command pipe and follows redirects/SSRF to internal hosts. Must parse/validate the URL and use URI.open with timeouts, not bare open.

findings.title: Nil feed item content crashes poller
findings.body: poll_feed does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assuming every RSS/Atom entry has content. Items with only link/title/description have nil content, raising NoMethodError and aborting the whole hourly poll so no items are imported.

findings.title: SSRF and unhandled fetch in import_remote
findings.body: import_remote does `open(url).read` on an embed_url supplied by any site visitor via EmbedController/TopicRetriever with no host allowlist check at this layer, no timeout, and no rescue. An attacker can make the server fetch internal hosts/files and a single failure or slow origin raises out of the Sidekiq job.

findings.title: Check-then-create race on embed_url unique index
findings.body: import does `where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction without handling concurrent creators. Two simultaneous retrieve_topic jobs for the same new URL both see blank and one raises RecordNotUnique on the unique index, failing the job instead of reusing the winner's row.

findings.title: Non-atomic throttle setnx+expire can leak key
findings.body: retrieved_recently? does `$redis.setnx(key,1)` then `$redis.expire(key,60)` as two commands. If the process crashes between them the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever. Use a single atomic SETEX/SET NX EX.

findings.title: Spec expects TopicRetriever but controller enqueues job
findings.body: EmbedController#best does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` while the spec mocks `TopicRetriever.new` and expects `retrieve`. The test does not verify actual behavior and will fail/pass for the wrong reason, leaving the loading path uncovered.
